corpus: AMI Meeting Corpus, manual annotations v1.6.2 and Mix-Headset audio (CC BY 4.0, AMI Consortium / University of Edinburgh)

questions.asking: Is the speaker asking a question?
questions.decision: Is the speaker making a decision?
questions.angry: Is the speaker angry or frustrated?
questions.company: Does the speaker name a company, product or brand?
questions.money: Does the speaker mention money or a price?
questions.person: Does the speaker mention a person by name?
questions.datetime: Does the speaker mention a date, a time or a deadline?
questions.place: Does the speaker mention a place?
questions.commit: Does the speaker commit to doing something?

method: Excerpts are 180 s windows from the 16 AMI-SDM evaluation meetings (EN2002, ES2004, IS1009, TS3003, a-d), five per meeting series.
The split is by meeting, never by excerpt: meetings a and c are the tuning half, b and d the held-out half, so each series appears in both halves and no meeting in both.

Windows in the annotated series (ES, IS, TS) were chosen greedily from 30 s steps to balance yes and no per question within each half; the EN2002 windows (no dialogue-act, entity or summary layers) were fixed at 600 s, 900 s and 1500 s.

'derived' is the label read from the annotations alone: asking = an Elicit-* dialogue act; decision / commit = an abstractive decisions / actions sentence linked to a dialogue act in the window (commit also on an Offer act); angry = a Be-Negative act; company = ORGANIZATION; money = MONEY; person = PERSON:OTHER or EXPERIMENTER; datetime = TIME or DATE; place = LOCATION.

'labels' is the final label, checked by reading each excerpt's transcript; every disagreement with 'derived', and every borderline call, has a note. 'The speaker' is read as anyone in the excerpt, since the meetings have four. Mentions of cost or expense count as money; named software products count as products.
Drafted by Claude (an LLM) on the user's request and not yet reviewed by a person.
